clue.text: Play very loudly after tea to tease

indicators.note: the word 'after' places the loud marking behind the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for a cup of tea
ff is the musical marking fortissimo, play very loudly

explanation.surface: Someone blasts music after teatime just to wind people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to banter with them, a light-hearted teasing.

clue.text: They describe circles in which business representative sits on fools

indicators.note: in a down answer, 'sits on' places the earlier pieces above the fools

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
asses are fools

explanation.surface: A company's MP perches on a bench of idiots, all of them going round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is the geometric sense: compasses describe, i.e. draw, circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of compasses is the drawing instrument used to trace a circle.

clue.text: The whole set of books, or portion

parts.note: all means the whole set
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Either the entire collection of volumes or just a share of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To portion something out is to distribute or assign shares of it.

clue.text: Get together German and British articles accepted by the festival

indicators.note: being accepted by the fete means sitting inside that word

parts.note: a fete is a festival or fair
der is a German definite article
a is the English indefinite article

explanation.surface: German and British goods are taken in at a fair, bringing nations together.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to unite into a league or federation.

clue.text: A six-footer goes around quietly or he checks out

indicators.note: the insect goes around the quiet letter, enclosing it

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so is a six-footer
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A very tall man prowls about softly, or perhaps he is the one investigating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines and checks things.

clue.text: Being single, was off like a shot for the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, single
ran means hurried away fast

explanation.surface: A lone person dashed off out of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Breaking the A-string possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A violinist's top string snaps mid-performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges THE plus ASTRING; the musical surface even suggests a snapping string.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattering means smashing into pieces, breaking violently.

clue.text: A Northerner needs some warm clothes — kimonos won't do

indicators.note: some means just a part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Someone in the Arctic needs thick garments; light Japanese robes are no use.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskimo is an older name for an Inuit or Yupik person of the far north.

clue.text: Goods vehicle entrance?

explanation.surface: A lorry pulls through a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport carries freight; to transport also means to enrapture, to entrance (verb).

clue.text: A rebel in flight

explanation.surface: An insurgent is on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises up is a rebel; a riser is also the upright part of a step in a staircase.

clue.text: Play with moral made to appear otherwise

indicators.note: made to appear otherwise means the letters are shown in a different order

explanation.surface: A drama whose message is twisted into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage piece with exaggerated characters.

clue.text: A writer's week-end food

parts.note: the end of 'week' is its last letter K
eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: An author's meals for Saturday and Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was a celebrated English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Rest an injured back

indicators.note: injured suggests the letters are damaged and put out of order

explanation.surface: Advice to lie still with a hurt back.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word for at or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: Note to the fellow keen to economise : spray

parts.note: A is a musical note
taken as written
a miser is a stingy person keen to save money

explanation.surface: A memo to a penny-pincher about a scent bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid into a fine mist.

clue.text: To back the worker isn't new

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: Supporting an employee who is no novice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase standing for the adjective: something second-hand is not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been previously owned, so are used rather than fresh.

clue.text: Little intended?

parts.note: read as a tender name for a beloved fiance, a dear little one someone means to marry

explanation.surface: Was this barely planned?
explanation.definitionFit: Intended is a dated term for fiance, a beloved partner.

clue.text: One reckons to smear it all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place shows the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone decides to smudge paint everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimator calculates likely costs or values, someone who reckons.

clue.text: Intimidates bovine creatures

explanation.surface: Cattle frighten people.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow is to bully into submission; cows are female cattle.

clue.text: This is killing! There's point to the hilarity

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
laughter is hilarity

explanation.surface: A joke so funny it kills, and there is a purpose in all the merriment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' looks like hilarious; the answer is the literal sense, mass killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is the brutal killing of many.

clue.text: He really doesn't like investigation into animals

indicators.note: into means the test goes inside the word for animals

parts.note: deer are animals
a test is an investigation or examination

explanation.surface: An opponent of animal experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loathes something intensely is one who hates it.

clue.text: The place is turned over by the extremists

indicators.note: turned over means the little word is flipped back to front
the extremists are the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A location is overturned by militants.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or spot.

clue.text: Wrong site in a pot plant

indicators.note: wrong indicates the letters are set out incorrectly and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A plant placed in the wrong container.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red bracts, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Distant — restraining anger as being more reasonable

indicators.note: restraining means the word for distant holds the anger within it

parts.note: far means distant
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Being aloof and keeping one's temper makes one more even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer means more just and even-handed.

clue.text: Forces man to order the duck

parts.note: to command is to order
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to go and get the duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier in an elite military raiding unit.

clue.text: Going up and down in town

indicators.note: going up and down says the letters read the same either way in a down entry

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Bustling about town.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town and its affairs.

clue.text: Giving chops to a male member of the team

parts.note: he refers to a male
a wing is a player on a team's flank

explanation.surface: A footballer passes the ball by chopping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing is cutting with blows of an axe, delivering chops.

clue.text: A figure initially thought perfect

indicators.note: initially means the thought is placed at the start, before the numeral

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a figure

explanation.surface: A body seems flawless at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Ready for some sport

explanation.surface: Prepared to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means willing or up for it; a game is also a sporting contest, and hunted animals are game.

clue.text: Choosy individual making his mark

parts.note: a person choosing a candidate puts a cross on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A fussy person trying to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter chooses by marking a cross on a ballot paper.

clue.text: A piece intended to sound flat

parts.note: a part is a piece

indicators.note: to sound means the word is spoken and its sound written down

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A section designed to be played in a flat key.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms for living in.

clue.text: Transport to the crest for the start of the shoot

parts.note: a cart is a means of transport
a ridge is a crest of a hill

explanation.surface: Carrying guns up to the hilltop before a day's shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is the casing loaded into a gun before it fires.

clue.text: The governor must be absolutely straight

explanation.surface: A leader has to be completely honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country; a ruler is also a straight-edged measuring strip.
